g.text: Why a bigger J++ part costs the 27B lookup: can't tell
Three causes, fixed in advance (below); none holds on the 27B. Extra loss (0-1): switches lost without
the J++ part, minus those lost without a random part (same size).
(1) The lens reads identity: from 25 to 100 directions identity answers fall 0.31 beyond the random part,
but position answers fall 0.11 too (bar: under 0.1). (2) The lens reads the pointer: the 100 directions
overlap it little (mean cos² 0.02; with identity, the two items' mean difference, 0.29). (3) Any 100
directions would do: another scene's cost the 27B lookup −0.01 [−0.04, 0.00] in the main test.
